ACCEPT. The extension’s written proof is valid under the stated feasibility and residual-count definitions. It removes the pressure, degree, and tree assumptions on unmarked tiles; the deficient-only surplus, internal attachment term, and corrected parity account exactly for what changes.Both explicit counterexamples are correct, and the connected bent-path construction works for every  $\ell\ge1$ . They refute the specified naive regional compensation rules. Their whole-grid objectives remain strictly below  $mn/2$ .1. The deficient-only surplus permits removal of ordinary pressureFirst, feasibility excludes three selected corners in any tile, since one would have two selected internal neighbors. Thus the deficient and saturated cases exhaust all tiles.For a deficient tile, the argument needs no pressure:If  $t=0$ , then  $b-t=b\ge0$ .If  $t=1$ , at least one of the selected corner’s two internal neighbors must be blank, giving  $b-t\ge0$ .For a marked tile, take its  $BB$  cap as the bottom face. Each of the two remaining corners has an occupied external neighbor across a perpendicular pressured face. They cannot both be selected; if one is selected, the other must be blank. Consequently the marked tile is deficient and contributes at least two to  $b-t$ .Since the marked tiles are distinct,
$$\boxed{D(R)\ge2L.}$$
The restriction to deficient tiles is necessary. An unpressured saturated tile can have two selected vertices, one matching endpoint, and one blank, giving  $b-t=-1$ . Excluding that negative contribution from  $D$ , then accounting for its matching attachment separately, is the correct replacement for ordinary pressure.No property of the adjacency graph of  $R$  enters this argument. Thick regions, degree-four tiles, and disconnected regions are covered whenever the marked tiles satisfy their stated local hypotheses.2. The saturated facts and  $Q=k+\eta$  are correctA saturated tile has at most one matching endpoint:Adjacent selected corners force both remaining corners blank.With diagonal selected corners, both remaining corners cannot be occupied.Writing  $p$  for its endpoint count therefore gives
$$p\le1,\qquad b=2-p,\qquad t-b=p.$$
In particular, a saturated tile cannot contain an internal matching edge.The exclusion of a matching edge between two saturated tiles is also valid in every physical orientation. Such an edge would join their unique  $P$  corners. Each tile would have diagonal selected corners, so the companion vertices on the shared face would both be selected. Each companion would have two occupied neighbors: its internal  $P$  corner and the selected companion across the face. That contradicts feasibility.Every saturated endpoint in  $R$  consequently has a deficient mate. Its matching edge either stays in  $R$ , contributing once to  $k$ , or leaves  $R$ , contributing once to  $\eta$ . Hence
$$\boxed{Q=k+\eta.}$$
There is no endpoint or edge counted twice.3. The exact ledger and corrected parity both check outFor a deficient tile, retain the full physical crossing count  $c$ . From
$$4=t+b+2h+c,\qquad d=c-s,$$
one obtains
$$\begin{aligned}
2\rho
&=d-2(2-t-h-s)\\
&=c+s-4+2t+2h\\
&=t-b+s.
\end{aligned}$$
When summed over deficient tiles in  $R$ , the  $s$ -incidences count exactly:deficient-inside to saturated-inside edges, once each in  $k$ ;deficient-inside to saturated-outside edges, once each in  $\sigma$ .Saturated tiles contribute zero charge. Thus
$$\boxed{2\rho(R)=-D(R)+k+\sigma.}$$
An  $\eta$ -edge has its deficient endpoint outside  $R$ , so it contributes no  $s$ -incidence to this sum. There is no missing incoming correction. The alternative calculation confirms the cancellation:
$$t-b+\sigma-\eta
=-D+Q+\sigma-\eta
=-D+k+\sigma.$$
For parity, summing the saturated identity  $b-t=-p$  gives
$$b-t=D-Q,\qquad D=b-t+Q.$$
The matching vertex partition
$$4|R_{\rm tiles}|=t+b+2\mu+j$$
therefore implies
$$\boxed{D\equiv j+Q\pmod2.}$$
Combining this with  $D\ge2L$  yields
$$D\ge2L+\bigl((j+Q)\bmod2\bigr),$$
and hence the claimed bound
$$\boxed{
2\rho(R)\le
-2L+k+\sigma-\bigl((j+Q)\bmod2\bigr).
}$$
As an additional check on all boundary directions, let  $j_{DD}$  count physical boundary matching edges between two deficient tiles. Since saturated-to-saturated edges are impossible,
$$j=j_{DD}+\sigma+\eta,$$
so
$$(j+Q)\bmod2
=(j_{DD}+\sigma+k+2\eta)\bmod2
=(j_{DD}+\sigma+k)\bmod2.$$
Incoming saturated endpoints do not independently generate a parity resource.Capacity-two tilesThe same ledger covers them without any allocation per residual visit. If  $r=2$ , nonnegativity of the counts in  $r=2-t-h-s$  forces
$$t=h=s=0,
\qquad
2\rho=-b.$$
A four-crossing tile with  $b=0$  contributes zero charge. Multiple residual passages through that tile do not create multiple surplus budgets.4. Source aggregation and the global sufficient class are validFor pairwise tile-disjoint  $R,U_1,\ldots,U_k$ , with charges fixed by the original configuration,
$$\rho\!\left(R\cup\bigcup_iU_i\right)
=\rho(R)+\sum_i\rho(U_i).$$
Using  $\sum_i\rho(U_i)\le L$  gives exactly
$$2\rho\!\left(R\cup\bigcup_iU_i\right)
\le k+\sigma-\bigl((j+Q)\bmod2\bigr).$$
This remains true when matching edges connect sources to one another or to the receiver. In particular, if an  $\eta$ -edge ends at a deficient tile in a source, that tile’s attachment contribution is already included in the stipulated source charge. The receiver’s cancellation of  $\eta$  supplies no extra source allowance.Accordingly,
$$k+\sigma\le (j+Q)\bmod2$$
is a valid sufficient condition for compensating the entire source aggregate. The case  $k=\sigma=0$  needs no bound on  $\eta$ .The no-reuse requirements are adequate: the surplus is summed over disjoint deficient tiles, every internal attachment contributes once, each receiver appears once, and distinct compensated cores must be disjoint as whole tile sets. Shared external pressure witnesses do not duplicate internal surplus.For the full rectangle, there are no exterior attachments, so  $Q=k$ . The exact ledger becomes
$$2\sum_{\rm tiles}\rho=-D+Q=t-b.$$
Since
$$mn=t+b+2|M|,$$
this proves
$$\sum_{\rm tiles}\rho
=|T|+|M|-\frac{mn}{2}.$$
Nonpositive disjoint cores and a nonpositive deficient remainder therefore give the claimed whole-grid inequality on the specified class. Saturated remainder tiles have zero charge.Finally, pressure on every tile forces  $Q=0$ . Then  $Q=k+\eta$  gives  $k=\eta=0$ , recovering the previous theorem and its  $j\bmod2$  correction exactly.5. Both explicit counterexamples have the stated countsA. The parity witness, including the marked-terminal variantThe original receiver tile  $(2,5)$  has labels
$$\begin{matrix}
T&P\\
B&T
\end{matrix}.$$
Both selected vertices have exactly the one occupied neighbor  $(4,11)$ . Its mate  $(4,12)$  lies in the deficient tile  $(2,6)$ . Therefore
$$Q=\eta=j=1,\qquad k=\sigma=D=0,\qquad \rho(R)=0.$$
The uncorrected parity bound would give  $2\rho\le-1$ , which is false. The corrected parity is even and gives equality.The additional tile  $(2,2)$  has labels
$$\begin{matrix}
B&P\\
B&P
\end{matrix}.$$
Its  $P$  vertices are matched internally, its left face is  $BB$ , and the listed matching edges in rows  $3$  and  $6$  make both perpendicular faces genuinely pressured. It has
$$t=0,\quad b=2,\quad h=1,\quad c=s=d=0,\quad r=1,\quad \rho=-1.$$
The pressure-producing edges are wholly outside  $R$ , so they do not change  $j$ . Thus the enlarged receiver has
$$L=1,\quad D=2,\quad \rho(R)=-1,\quad Q=\eta=j=1,\quad k=\sigma=0.$$
The old parity formula incorrectly gives  $2\rho\le-3$ ; the new one gives  $-2$  exactly.The complete matching endpoint lists are disjoint, and the added endpoints do not alter the original selected vertices’ occupied-neighbor counts.B. The internal-debt witnessThe two tiles have labels
$$\begin{matrix}
T&P\\
B&T
\end{matrix}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\begin{matrix}
P&P\\
B&T
\end{matrix}.$$
The first is saturated. In the second,
$$t=b=1,\qquad h=0,\qquad c=2,\qquad s=1,$$
because one matching edge joins the saturated first tile and the other exits upward into a deficient tile. Hence
$$r=0,\qquad d=1,\qquad \rho=\frac12.$$
All three selected vertices have exactly one occupied neighbor, as stated.The regional counts are therefore
$$Q=k=j=1,\qquad \eta=\sigma=D=0,\qquad 2\rho(R)=1.$$
The corrected parity is even, and the new bound is exact. Replacing the coefficient of  $k$  in that bound by any constant  $a<1$ , while retaining the other terms, would require  $1\le a$ . This proves the asserted sharpness of that coefficient.These witnesses are far below the global target:| Configuration in the  $10\times16$  rectangle |  $|T|+|M|$  |  $mn/2$  ||---|---:|---:|| Single parity tile |  $3$  |  $80$  || Parity tile plus marked terminal |  $6$  |  $80$  || Two-tile internal-debt gadget |  $5$  |  $80$  |They are counterexamples to the specified regional estimates, with no global violation.6. The connected bent-path obstruction works at every lengthWrite
$$A=(1,1),\qquad B=(1,2),\qquad
V_c=(0,c)\quad(2\le c\le\ell+1)$$
for the tiles in  $R$ .Matching legality and feasibilityThe endpoint families are disjoint:The original edges use  $(2,3),(2,4),(2,5),(1,5)$ .The added vertical edge uses  $(0,4),(1,4)$ .The bottom-row internal pairs use row  $1$ , columns  $6,\ldots,2\ell+3$ .The top-row crossing pairs use row  $0$ , columns  $5,\ldots,2\ell+4$ .Every edge joins adjacent grid vertices. The final endpoint  $(0,2\ell+4)$  lies inside the  $6\times(2\ell+8)$  rectangle.The three selected vertices retain exactly these occupied neighbors:
$$(2,2)\mapsto(2,3),\qquad
(3,3)\mapsto(2,3),\qquad
(3,5)\mapsto(2,5).$$
Their other neighbors remain blank.At  $\ell=1$ , the family indexed by  $3\le c\le\ell+1$  is empty, as required. The construction remains valid.Induced geometry and tile chargesThe induced adjacency graph has precisely
$$A-B,\qquad B-V_2,\qquad
V_c-V_{c+1}\quad(2\le c\le\ell).$$
It is a path on  $\ell+2$  tiles. For  $\ell=1$ , it is already a three-tile right-angle path; for larger  $\ell$ , it continues across the upper row.In  $V_2$ , the vertical edge is internal, while the remaining endpoints belong to the incoming edge from  $B$  and the outgoing top-row edge. For  $c\ge3$ , the bottom pair is internal, and the two top endpoints belong to the incoming and outgoing crossings. Thus every upper tile satisfies
$$t=b=s=0,\qquad h=1,\qquad c=d=2,\qquad r=1,\qquad \rho=0.$$
The sole boundary matching edge is
$$(0,2\ell+3)--(0,2\ell+4),$$
which enters the outside deficient tile  $V_{\ell+2}$ . It remains included in the last receiver tile’s residual degree. This retention of the outgoing boundary edge is essential to the stated zero charge.Therefore, at every length,
$$\boxed{
k=Q=j=1,\qquad D=\eta=\sigma=0,\qquad \rho(R)=\frac12.
}$$
The residual route begins at  $B$ , travels upward and then along the upper row, and exits  $R$ . The saturated attachment  $A-B$  is the single internal debt and is excluded from that residual route.Whole-grid objectiveThe total number of matching edges is
$$2+1+(\ell-1)+\ell=2\ell+2.$$
Consequently,
$$|T|+|M|=2\ell+5,
\qquad
\frac{mn}{2}=6\ell+24,$$
with strict difference
$$\frac{mn}{2}-(|T|+|M|)=4\ell+19>0.$$
This establishes the all-length regional obstruction: extending the displayed receiving route preserves its positive half-unit charge. The family does not satisfy the compensation criterion, since  $k+\sigma=1$  while  $(j+Q)\bmod2=0$ , and it does not violate the global inequality.No mathematical revision is required. This verdict covers the written extension and the explicit constructions; it does not rely on the earlier ACCEPT or on the reported finite and Lean checks.
